1333.subject: Physics
1333.text:
Assertion : A bird perches on a high power line and nothing happens to the bird.
Reason : The level of bird is very high from the ground.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1333.sol: Electric shock is due to the electric current flowing through a living body. When the bird perches on a single high power line, no current passes through its body because its body is at equipotential surface i.e., there is no potential difference. While when man touches the same line, standing bare foot on ground the electrical circuit is completed through the ground. The hands of man are at high potential and his feets are at low potential. Hence large amount of current flows through the body of the man and person therefore gets a fatal shock.
1333.meta: Assertion : A bird perches on a high power line and nothing happens to the bird. Reason : The level of bird is very high from the ground.

10413.text: On an \(n \times n\) chessboard, the total number of rectangles which are not squares is 350. Then, the number of white squares on the chessboard is.......
10413.sol:
Number of rectangles in a chess board
(including squares) \(=\Sigma n³\)
\(=\frac{n^2(n+1)^2}{4}\)
Number of squares in a chess board
\(=\Sigma n²=\frac{n(n+1)(2 n+1)}{6}\)
So, Number of rectangles which are not squares
$$\begin{aligned}&=\Sigma n³-\Sigma n² \\
&=\frac{n^2(n+1)^2}{4}-  n \frac{(n+1)(2 n+1)}{6}=350 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad n\left(\frac{n+1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}-\frac{2 n+1}{3}\right)=350
\end{aligned}$$\)
$$\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow& & n \left(\frac{n+1}{2}\right)  \ left(\frac{3 n²+3 n-4 n-2}{6}\right)& =350 \\
\Rightarrow &   n(n+1)\left(3 n²-n-2\right) & =350 \times6 \times2 \\
\Rightarrow &   n(n+1)\left(3 n²-3 n+2 n-2\right)& =350 \times6 \times2 \\
\Rightarrow & & n(n+1)(3 n(n-1)+2(n-1) & =350 \times6 \times2 \\
\Rightarrow & & n(n+1)(n-1)(3 n+2) & =350 \times6 \times2 \\
\Rightarrow & & (n-1) n(n+1)(3 n+2) & =5 \times6 \times7 \times20
\end{aligned}$$\)
By comparison we get
\(\therefore \quad n=6\)
Hence, total number of black and white squares
\(=n \timesn=6 \times6=36\)
Half of there are
\(\text{white }=\frac{36}{2}=18 \text{ squares. }\)

11391.text: If the bi-quadratic equation $f ( x ) = x^{4} + 2x^{3} - 16x^{2} - 22x + 7 = 0$ has $2 + \sqrt{3}$ as one of its roots, then which of the following is not a root of $f\left(x\right) ?$
11391.sol:
Given,& $f ( x ) = x^{4} + 2x^{3} - 16x^{2} - 22x + 7 = 0$

$∵ 2 + \sqrt{3}$ is one of the roots of& $f\left(x\right) = 0$

$∴ 2 - \sqrt{3}$ is also one of the roots of& $f\left(x\right) = 0$

Let us assume the other two roots of the $f\left(x\right) = 0$ are& $\alpha, \beta$

$⇒$ Sum of roots$= - 2$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + 2 + \sqrt{3} + 2 - \sqrt{3} = - 2$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta = - 6 \ldots \left(i\right)$

And product of roots$= 7$

$⇒ \alpha\beta \left(2 + \sqrt{3}\right)\left(2 - \sqrt{3}\right) =7$

$⇒ \alpha\beta =7 \ldots \left(ii\right)$

Put \beta = $\dfrac{7}{\alpha}$ in equation& $\left(i\right)$, we get

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} + 6\alpha +7 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{- 6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 28}}{2} = -3 \pm \sqrt{2}

Put value$ of \alpha in$equation& \left(ii\right), we get

$\beta = -3 ∓ \sqrt{2}

$∴$ Roots of the& $f\left(x\right) = 0$ are& $2 + \sqrt{3},2 - \sqrt{3}, -3 + \sqrt{2}, -3 - \sqrt{2}.

Then, $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=a, \alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha=b$ and $\alpha \beta \gamma=c$.
Now, $\Sigma \alpha^2(\beta+\gamma)=\Sigma \alpha^2(a-\alpha)$
[as $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=a]$
$\begin{aligned}$& =a $\sum \alpha^$2-$\sum \alpha^$3 \\
& =a$\left[(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^$2-2($\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha)\right]-[(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)$\\
& $\left.\quad\left(\alpha^$2+$\beta^$2+$\gamma^$2-$\alpha \beta-\beta \gamma-\gamma \alpha\right)+$3 $\alpha \beta \gamma\right]$\\
& =a$\left[(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^$2-2($\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha)\right]-(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)$\\
& \quad$\left\{($\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^$2-3($\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha)+$3 $\alpha \beta \gamma\right]$\\
& =a$\left[$a^2-2 b\right]-$\left[$a$\left\{a^2-3 b\right\}+3 c\right] \\
& =a³-2 a b-a³+3 a b-3 c=a b-3 c
\end{aligned}

11776.text: The random variable takes the values $1,2,3$, $\ldots, m$. If $P(X=n)=\frac{1}{m}$ to each $n$, then the variance of $X$ is
11776.sol: $\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{var}(X)=\sum_{i=2}^{\infty} P_i\left(X_i-\bar{X}\right)^2 \\ & \bar{X}=\frac{1+2+\ldots+m}{m}=\frac{m(m+1)}{2 \cdot m}=\frac{m+1}{2} \\ & \operatorname{var}(X)=\{P(X=1)+P(X=2)+\ldots+P(X=m)\} \\ & =\left\{\frac{1}{m}\left(1-\frac{m+1}{2}\right)^2+\frac{1}{m}\left(2-\frac{m+1}{2}\right)^2+\ldots+\frac{1}{m}\right. \\ & =\frac{1}{m}\left\{\left(1^2+\frac{(m+1)^2}{4}-2 \cdot 1\left(\frac{m+1}{2}\right)\right)\right. \\ & \quad+\left(2^2+\frac{(m+1)^2}{4}-2 \cdot 2 \frac{m+1}{2}\right)+\ldots \\ & \left.\quad+\left(m^2+\frac{(m+1)^2}{4}-m \cdot 2 \frac{(m+1)}{2}\right)\right\} \\ & =\frac{1}{m}\left\{\left(1^2+2^2+\ldots+m^2\right)+\frac{(m+1)^2}{4}(1+1+\ldots\right. \\ & \quad+m \text{ times) }-(m+1)(1+2+3+\ldots+m)\} \\ & \left.=\frac{1}{12}\right\} \\ & =\frac{1}{12}\left\{\frac{m(m+1)(2 m+1)}{6}+\frac{m(m+1)^2}{4}\right. \\ & =\frac{(m+1)[2(2 m+1)+3(m+1)-6 m+1]}{2}\end{aligned}$

Let the slope of line $m$ and $m_1$ of the equation

Then, $m+m_2=\frac{b}{3}$ and $m m_2=-2 / 3$

$\therefore \quad \frac{m m_1}{m m_2}=-1\Rightarrow \quad m_1=-m_2\Rightarrow \quad m_1+m_2=0$...(ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$m_1=1$ and $m_2=-1\therefore \quad m=2 / 3m+m_1=-a / 3\Rightarrow \quad \frac{2}{3}+1=-a / 3 \Rightarrow a=-5$
and $m+m_2=b / 3\Rightarrow \quad \frac{2}{3}-1=b / 3 \Rightarrow b=-1\therefore \quad a=-5$ and $b=-1$

14303.text: A magnetic field given by $B(t)=\left(0.2 t-0.05 t^2\right) T$ is directed perpendicular to the plane of a circular coil containing 25 turns of radius $1.8 \mathrm{ cm}$ and whose total resistance is $5 \Omega$. The power dissipation at $3 \mathrm{ s}$ is nearly

Radius of coil, $r=1.8 \mathrm{ cm}=1.8 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{ m}$ Resistance of coil, $R=5 \Omega$
Magnetic field, $B=\left(0.2 t-0.05 t^2\right) \mathrm{T}$
Now, area of coil,
$\begin{aligned} A & =\pi r^2=3.14 \times\left(1.8 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \\ & =1.02 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ m}^2\end{aligned}$
Induced emf, $\varepsilon=\frac{-N d}{d t}(B A)=-N A \frac{d B}{d t}\begin{aligned} & =-N A \frac{d}{d t}\left(0.2 t-0.05 t^2\right) \\ \varepsilon & =-N A(0.2-0.1 t)\end{aligned}$
Substituting the values, we get
$\begin{aligned} \varepsilon & =-25 \times 1.02 \times 10^{-3}(0.2-0.1 t) \\ & =-2.55 \times 10^{-2}(0.2-0.1 t)\end{aligned}$
Now, instantaneous power,
$P=\frac{\varepsilon^2}{R}=\frac{\left[-2.55 \times 10^{-2}(0.2-0.1 t)\right]^2}{5}$
At, $t=3 \mathrm{ s}$, power dissipated is
$P=\frac{\left(2.55 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2(0.2-0.1 \times 3)^2}{5}=1.30 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{ W}=1.30 \mu \mathrm{W}$
It is close to option (d).

17749.sol:

19909.subject: Chemistry
19909.text: At $300 \mathrm{ K}$, the half-life period of a gaseous reaction at an initial pressure of $40 \mathrm{ kPa}$ is 350 s. When pressure is $20 \mathrm{ kPa}$, the half-life period is 175 s. What is the order of the reaction?
19909.sol:
For a gaseous reaction of order $n$, the half-life $t_{1/2}$ is related to the initial pressure $P_0$ by the relation $t_{1/2} \propto \dfrac{1}{P_0^{n-1}}$.

Given data:
Case 1: $P_{0,1} = 40 \text{ kPa}$, $t_{1/2,1} = 350 \text{ s}$
Case 2: $P_{0,2} = 20 \text{ kPa}$, $t_{1/2,2} = 175 \text{ s}$

Taking the ratio of the two cases:
$\dfrac{t_{1/2,1}}{t_{1/2,2}} = \left( \dfrac{P_{0,2}}{P_{0,1}} \right)^{n-1}$

Substituting the values:
$\dfrac{350}{175} = \left( \dfrac{20}{40} \right)^{n-1}$

$2 = \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^{n-1}$

$2 = (2^{-1})^{n-1}$

$2^1 = 2^{1-n}$

Equating the exponents:
$1 = 1 - n$

$n = 0$.

Answer: Zero

20463.text: In a $0.2 \mathrm{ M}$ aqueous solution, lactic acid is $6.9 \%$ dissociated. The value of dissociation constant is
20463.sol:
For a weak acid dissociation $HA \rightleftharpoons H^{+} + A^{-}$, the dissociation constant $K_a$ is given by the expression $K_a = \dfrac{c \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$.

Given concentration $c = 0.2 \text{ M}$ and degree of dissociation $\alpha = 6.9 \% = 0.069$.

Since $\alpha$ is small, we can approximate $1 - \alpha \approx 1$, so $K_a \approx c \alpha^2$.

Substituting the values: $K_a = 0.2 \times (0.069)^2$.

$K_a = 0.2 \times 0.004761 = 0.0009522$.

Expressing in scientific notation, $K_a = 9.522 \times 10^{-4} \approx 9.5 \times 10^{-4}$.

Answer: $9.5 \times 10^{-4}$

20940.subject: Mathematics
20940.text: If $f(x)=\log x+b x^2+a x, x \neq 0$ has extreme values (or turning points) at $x=-1$ and $x=2$ then the values of $\mathrm{a}$ and $\mathrm{b}$ are
20940.sol:
Given $f(x) = \log x + bx^2 + ax$. The derivative of the function is $f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{x} + 2bx + a$.

Since the function has extreme values at $x = -1$ and $x = 2$, $f'(x)$ must be zero at these points.

For $x = -1$: $f'(-1) = \dfrac{1}{-1} + 2b(-1) + a = 0 \Rightarrow -1 - 2b + a = 0 \Rightarrow a - 2b = 1$.

For $x = 2$: $f'(2) = \dfrac{1}{2} + 2b(2) + a = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2} + 4b + a = 0 \Rightarrow a + 4b = -\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Subtracting the first equation from the second: $(a + 4b) - (a - 2b) = -\dfrac{1}{2} - 1 \Rightarrow 6b = -\dfrac{3}{2} \Rightarrow b = -\dfrac{3}{12} = -\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Substituting $b = -\dfrac{1}{4}$ into $a - 2b = 1$: $a - 2(-\dfrac{1}{4}) = 1 \Rightarrow a + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1 \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Thus, $a = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $b = -\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Answer: $a=\dfrac{1}{2} \quad b=-\dfrac{1}{4}$

21325.subject: Mathematics
21325.text: The number of solutions of $\dfrac{d y}{d x}=\dfrac{y+1}{x-1}$, when $y(1)=2$ is
21325.sol:
The given differential equation is a first-order linear separable differential equation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y+1}{x-1}$.

Separating the variables, we have $\int \dfrac{dy}{y+1} = \int \dfrac{dx}{x-1}$.

Integrating both sides, we get $\ln|y+1| = \ln|x-1| + C$, which can be written as $y+1 = k(x-1)$ where $k$ is a constant.

The initial condition is given as $y(1) = 2$. Substituting $x=1$ and $y=2$ into the equation $y+1 = k(x-1)$, we get $2+1 = k(1-1)$, which simplifies to $3 = k(0)$.

Since $3 = 0$ is a contradiction, there is no value of $k$ that satisfies the initial condition $y(1) = 2$.

Therefore, there are zero solutions to the given differential equation with the specified initial condition.

Answer: zero

22603.subject: Physics
22603.text: Three bulbs of $40 \mathrm{ W}, 60 \mathrm{ W}$, and $100 \mathrm{ W}$ are arranged in series with a $220 \mathrm{ V}$ source. The maximum light is obtained from
22603.sol:
The power consumed by a bulb is given by $P = I^2 R$, where $I$ is the current flowing through the bulb and $R$ is its resistance. Since the bulbs are connected in series, the same current $I$ flows through all of them.

The resistance $R$ of a bulb is related to its rated power $P_{rated}$ and rated voltage $V$ by the formula $R = \dfrac{V^2}{P_{rated}}$.

For the given bulbs:
$R_{40} = \dfrac{V^2}{40}$
$R_{60} = \dfrac{V^2}{60}$
$R_{100} = \dfrac{V^2}{100}$

Comparing the resistances, we find $R_{40} > R_{60} > R_{100}$.

Since $P = I^2 R$ and $I$ is constant for all bulbs in series, the power consumed by each bulb is directly proportional to its resistance. Therefore, the bulb with the highest resistance will consume the most power and emit the most light.

Thus, the $40 \mathrm{ W}$ bulb has the highest resistance and will glow the brightest.

Answer: 40 W

23001.subject: Physics
23001.text: Two long parallel conductors X and Y are placed vertically at a distance d apart. Conductor X carries a current I upwards and conductor Y carries a current 2I downwards. A third long conductor Z is placed parallel to both X and Y and between X and Y. If Z carries a current I upwards and is at a distance $x$ from conductor X, then:
options: All the conductors are in equilibrium and the net force on Z is zero
The net force on Z is $\dfrac{\mu_0 I²}{2x\pi} \left[\dfrac{d+x}{d-x}\right]$towards X
The net force on Z is $\dfrac{\mu_0 I²}{2x\pi} \left[\dfrac{d+x}{d-x}\right]$towards Y
The net force on Z is $\dfrac{\mu_0 I²}{2x\pi} \left[\dfrac{d-x}{d+x}\right]$towards Y
23001.sol:
The force per unit length between two parallel current-carrying wires is given by $F = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi r}$.

Wires carrying current in the same direction attract each other, while wires carrying current in opposite directions repel each other.

The force per unit length on wire Z due to wire X is:
$F_{ZX} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I \cdot I}{2\pi x} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi x}$
Since the currents in X and Z are in the same direction (upwards), this force is attractive. Therefore, $F_{ZX}$ is directed towards X.

The force per unit length on wire Z due to wire Y is:
$F_{ZY} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I \cdot 2I}{2\pi (d-x)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 2I^2}{2\pi (d-x)}$
Since the currents in Y and Z are in opposite directions (Y is downwards, Z is upwards), this force is repulsive. Therefore, $F_{ZY}$ is directed away from Y, which is also towards X.

The net force per unit length on wire Z is the sum of these two forces, as they act in the same direction:
$F_{net} = F_{ZX} + F_{ZY}$

$F_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi x} + \dfrac{\mu_0 2I^2}{2\pi (d-x)}$

$F_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi} \left[ \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{2}{d-x} \right]

$ F_{net} = $\dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi} \left[ \dfrac{d - x + 2x}{x(d-x)} \right]<$ br>
$F_{net} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I²}{2\pi x} \left[ \dfrac{d+x}{d-x} \right]$

The direction of the net force is towards X.

Answer: The net force on Z is $\dfrac{\mu_0 I²}{2x\pi} \left[\dfrac{d+x}{d-x}\right]$ towards X

\Rightarrow \quad t &=\frac{2 u \pm \sqrt{4 u^{2}-4 g \times 2 h}}{2 g}\\
&=\frac{u \pm \sqrt{u^{2}-2 g h}}{g}

26813.subject: Chemistry
26813.text: Arrange the following compounds according to increasing order of boiling points. $n\text{-}\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$ (A), $n\text{-}\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{NH}_2$ (B), $n\text{-}\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$ (C) and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NHC}_2\text{H}_5$ (D).
26813.sol:
Boiling point depends on the strength of intermolecular forces.

$n\text{-C}_4\text{H}_{10}$ (C) is a nonpolar alkane with only weak van der Waals forces, resulting in the lowest boiling point.

$n\text{-C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$ (A) is an alcohol that forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds due to the high electronegativity of oxygen, giving it the highest boiling point.

Both $n\text{-C}_4\text{H}_9\text{NH}_2$ (B) and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NHC}_2\text{H}_5$ (D) are amines and form hydrogen bonds, which are weaker than those in alcohols because nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen.

Between the primary amine (B) and the secondary amine (D), the primary amine has two $\text{N-H}$ bonds available for hydrogen bonding and less steric hindrance, leading to stronger intermolecular forces and a higher boiling point than the secondary amine.

The increasing order of boiling points is $C < D < B < A$.

Answer: $C < D < B < A$

27407.subject: Chemistry
27407.text: Sucrose hydrolyses in acidic medium into glucose and fructose by first order rate law with $t_{1/2} = 3$ hour. The percentage of sucrose remaining after $6$ hours is _______. (Nearest integer) (Given: $\log 2 = 0.3010$ and $\log 3 = 0.4771$)
27407.sol:
For a first order reaction, the amount of reactant remaining after $n$ half-lives is given by $N_t = \dfrac{N_0}{2^n}$.

Given $t_{1/2} = 3$ hours and total time $t = 6$ hours.

Number of half-lives, $n = \dfrac{t}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2$.

The amount of sucrose remaining is $N_t = \dfrac{N_0}{2^2} = \dfrac{N_0}{4}$.

Percentage of sucrose remaining $= \dfrac{N_t}{N_0} \times 100 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 100 = 25$.

Answer: $25$

32172.sol:
For case (A) with n=5, $m_l=-1$:
The principal quantum number n=5 allows l from 0 to 4. Since $m_l=-1$, we need l≥1. For each l value (1, 2, 3, 4), the orbital $m_l=-1$ exists, giving 4 orbitals. Each orbital holds 2 electrons (spin up and down), so maximum electrons = 8.
For case (B) with n=3, l=2, $m_l=-1$, $m_s=+\frac{1}{2}$:
These quantum numbers completely specify a single electron in a unique orbital with a specific spin, so maximum electrons = 1.
Therefore, the answer is 8 and 1.

maximum $f(x)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}}$

$f(c)=\frac{1}{3}$

36831.text: The sum of all the roots of the equation $(x-1)^{2}-5|x-1|+6=0$, is :
36831.sol:
Let $t = |x-1|$ where $t \geq 0$.
Equation becomes $t^2 - 5t + 6 = 0$.
$(t-2)(t-3) = 0$ gives $t = 2$ or $t = 3$.
For $|x-1| = 2$: $x = 3$ or $x = -1$.
For $|x-1| = 3$: $x = 4$ or $x = -2$.
Sum of roots $= 3 + (-1) + 4 + (-2) = 4$.

37642.text:
Let $\mathrm{x}_1, \mathrm{x}_2, \ldots \ldots, \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{n}}$ be $\mathrm{n}$ observations, and let $\overline{\mathrm{x}}$ be their arithematic mean and $\sigma^2$ be their variance. 
Statement $1$: Variance of $2 x_1, 2 x_2, \ldots \ldots, 2 x_n$ is $4 \sigma^2$.
Statement $2$: Arithmetic mean of $2 \mathrm{x}_1, 2 \mathrm{x}_2, \ldots . ., 2 \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{n}}$ is $4 \overline{\mathrm{x}}$.
options:
Statement $1$ is false, statement $2$ is true

Statement $1$ is true, statement $2$ is true; statement $2$ is a correct explanation for statement $1$

Statement $1$ is true, statement $2$ is true; statement $2$ is not a correct explanation for statement $1$

Statement $1$ is true, statement $2$ is false
37642.sol:
$\sigma^2=\sum \frac{x_i^2}{n}-\left(\sum \frac{x_i}{n}\right)^2$
Variance of $2 x_1, 2 x_2, \ldots . ., 2 x_n=\sum \frac{\left(2 x_i\right)^2}{n}-\left(\sum \frac{2 x_i}{n}\right)^2=4\left[\sum \frac{x_i^2}{n}-\left(\sum \frac{x_i}{n}\right)^2\right]=4 \sigma^2$ Statement $1$ is true.
A.M. of $2 x_1, 2 x_2, \ldots \ldots, 2 x_n=\frac{2 x_1+2 x_2+\cdots+2 x_n}{n}=2\left(\frac{x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n}{n}\right)=2 \bar{x}$
Statement $2$ is false.

38007.text: Let the foot of perpendicular from the point $A\left(4, 3, 1\right)$ on the plane $P: x - y + 2z + 3 = 0$ be $N$. If $B ( 5, \alpha, \beta ) , \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{Z}$ is a point on plane $P$ such that the area of the triangle $ABN$ is $3\sqrt{2}$, then ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} + \alpha\beta$ is equal to _____________
38007.sol:
Given,

The foot of perpendicular from the point $A\left(4, 3, 1\right)$ on the plane $P: x - y + 2z + 3 = 0$ be $N$

So, by foot of perpendicular formula we get,

$\dfrac{{x}_{1} - 4}{1} = \dfrac{{y}_{1} - 3}{- 1} = \dfrac{{z}_{1} - 1}{2} = - \dfrac{4 - 3 + 2 + 3}{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {2}^{2}}$

$⇒ N ≡ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right) = ( 3, 4, - 1 )$

And $B\left(5, \alpha, \beta\right), \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{Z}$ is a point on plane $P$ such that the area of the triangle $ABN$ is $3\sqrt{2}$,

So putting the value of point $B\left(5, \alpha, \beta\right)$ in plane we get,

$5 - \alpha + 2\beta + 3 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha - 2\beta = 8$

And given area of triangle $ABN$ is $3\sqrt{2}$, we get

$\dfrac{1}{2}AN \times BN = 3\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ AN \times BN = 6\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{6}} \times BN = 6\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ BN = 2\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ 4 + {\left(\alpha - 4\right)}^{2} + {\left(\beta + 1\right)}^{2} = 12$

$⇒ {\left(\alpha - 4\right)}^{2} + {\left(\beta + 1\right)}^{2} = 8$

$⇒ 5{\beta}^{2} + 18\beta + 9 = 0$ $\left\{\text{as}\alpha - 2\beta = 8\right\}$

$⇒ \beta = - 3\left\{\text{as}\beta \ne - \dfrac{3}{5}\right\}$

So, $\beta = - 3, \alpha = 2$

Hence, ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} + \alpha\beta = {3}^{2} + {2}^{2} - 6 = 7$

38077.text: The line of shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x - 2}{0} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x - 3}{2} = \dfrac{y - 5}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{1}$ makes an angle of $\sin^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{27}}\right)$ with the planeP: ax - y - z = 0, $\left(a > 0\right)$. If the image of the point $\left(1, 1, - 5\right)$ in the plane $P$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$, then $\alpha + \beta - \gamma$ is equal to _____ .
38077.sol:
Given lines, $\dfrac{x - 2}{0} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x - 3}{2} = \dfrac{y - 5}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{1}$

Now direction ratio of line of shortest distance will be,

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right| = - \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

Now given angle between line and plane is $\sin^{- 1}\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{27}} = \alpha$, so $sin\alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{27}}$

Now direction ratio of normal to plane is $\left(a, - 1, - 1\right)$

So, $sin\alpha = \left|\dfrac{- a - 2 + 2}{\sqrt{4 + 4 + 1}\sqrt{{a}^{2} + 1 + 1}}\right| = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ \sqrt{3}\left|a\right| = \sqrt{2}\sqrt{{a}^{2} + 2}$

$⇒ 3{a}^{2} = 2{a}^{2} + 4$

$⇒ {a}^{2} = 4$

$⇒ a = 2\left(\text{as}a > 0\text{given}\right)$

Now equation of plane will be $2x - y - z = 0$ and image of point $\left(1, 1, - 5\right)$ will be,

$\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z + 5}{- 1} = - 2\dfrac{\left(2 - 1 + 5\right)}{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z + 5}{- 1} = - 2$

$⇒ x = - 3, y = 3, z = - 3$

So, $\alpha = - 3, \beta = 3, \gamma = - 3$

So, $\alpha + \beta - \gamma = - 3 + 3 + 3 = 3$

38552.text: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$  and $\overset{\to}{c}$ is a vector such that $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) + 25 = 0, \overset{\to}{c} \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) = 4$ and projection of $\overset{\to}{c}$ on $\overset{\to}{a}$ is $1$ , then the projection of $\overset{\to}{c}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ equals:
38552.sol:
Given:

$\overset{\to}{a} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & - 4 & 5\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 15\overset{^}{i} - 20\overset{^}{j} - 25\overset{^}{k}$

Let $\overset{\to}{c} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$

Then,

$\overset{\to}{c} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) + 25 = 0$

$⇒ 15x - 20y - 25z + 25 = 0$

$⇒ 3x - 4y - 5z = - 5 . . . \left(1\right)$

Also,

$\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 4$

$⇒ x + y + z = 4 . . . . \left(2\right)$

And projection of $\overset{\to}{c}$ on $\overset{\to}{a}$ is

$\dfrac{\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}}{| \overset{\to}{a} |} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right)}{\sqrt{16 + 9}} = 1$

$⇒ 4x + 3y = 5 . . . . \left(3\right)$

Solving $\left(1\right), \left(2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$, we get

$x = 2, y = - 1, z = 3$

So,

$\overset{\to}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Projection of $\overset{\to}{c}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ is

$\dfrac{\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|} = \dfrac{\left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{9 + 16 + 25}} = \dfrac{25}{5\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}$

41413.text: The magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular loop of radius $R$ is $16 \mu \mathrm{~T}$. The magnetic field at a distance $x=\sqrt{3} R$ on its axis from the centre is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mu \mathrm{T}$.
41413.sol:
The magnetic field at the center of a circular loop is $B_{center} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R} = 16\mu$ T.
On the axis at distance $x$ from center: $B(x) = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$.
At $x = \sqrt{3}R$: $B(\sqrt{3}R) = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + 3R^2)^{3/2}} = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(4R^2)^{3/2}} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{16R}$.
The ratio: $\frac{B(\sqrt{3}R)}{B_{center}} = \frac{1/16R}{1/2R} = \frac{1}{8}$.
Therefore: $B(\sqrt{3}R) = \frac{1}{8} \times 16\mu = 2\mu$ T.

41883.subject: Physics
41883.text: The surface tension of a soap solution is $3.5 \times 10^{-2}$ N/m. The work required to increase the radius of a soap bubble from $1$ cm to $2$ cm is $\alpha \times 10^{-6}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is _____. ($\pi = 22/7$)
41883.sol:
The work done to increase the radius of a soap bubble is given by $W = T \times \Delta A$

Since a soap bubble has two free surfaces, the change in surface area is $\Delta A = 2 \times 4\pi (r_2^2 - r_1^2)$

Substituting the given values:

$W = 3.5 \times 10^{-2} \times 8\pi \times ((2 \times 10^{-2})^2 - (1 \times 10^{-2})^2)$

$W = 3.5 \times 10^{-2} \times 8\pi \times (4 \times 10^{-4} - 1 \times 10^{-4})$

$W = 3.5 \times 10^{-2} \times 8\pi \times 3 \times 10^{-4}$

$W = 84\pi \times 10^{-6}$

Using $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$:

$W = 84 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 10^{-6} = 264 \times 10^{-6}$ J

Comparing with $\alpha \times 10^{-6}$ J, we get $\alpha = 264$

Answer: $264$

42715.text: A mass $m$ attached to free end of a spring executes SHM with a period of $1s$. If the mass is increased by $3kg$ the period of oscillation increases by one second, the value of mass $m$ is ________ $kg$.
42715.sol:
Time period of oscillation is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$, where $k$ is the force constant of the spring.

$∵$ Spring is same, therefore, spring constant will be same.

Putting the different values,

In the first case $T = 1 = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$

In the second case ${T}^{'} = 2 = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m + 3}{k}}$

Dividing the equations, we get

$\dfrac{T}{{T}^{'}} = \dfrac{1}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{m + 3}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{m + 3} = \dfrac{1}{4} ⇒ 4m = m + 3 ⇒ m = 1$

Thus, $m = 1kg$

We also know that, kinetic energy is related to momentum as $KE = \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m}$.

Now, from both equations, we have

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{{A}_{1}}{{A}_{2}}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{{m}_{2}}{{m}_{1}} = \dfrac{1024}{900}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{A}_{1}}{{A}_{2}} = \dfrac{32}{30} = \dfrac{16}{15} = \dfrac{16}{16 - 1}$

$∴ \alpha = 16$

43908.text: A sample of an ideal gas is taken through the cyclic process $ABCA$ as shown in figure. It absorbs, $40J$ of heat during the part $AB$, no heat during $BC$ and rejects $60J$ of heat during $CA$. A work of $50J$ is done on the gas during the part $BC$. The internal energy of the gas at $A$ is $1560J$. The work done by the gas during the part $CA$ is
43908.sol:
In the part $A \to B$, the volume remains constant. Thus, the work done by the gas is zero. It is given that the heat absorbed by the gas is $40J$. From first law of thermodynamics, $Q = \DeltaU + W$

$⇒ 40 = \DeltaU + 0 ⇒ \DeltaU = 40J$

or $\DeltaU = {U}_{B} - {U}_{A} = 40J$

The increase in internal energy from $A$ to $B$ is $40J$. The internal energy is $1560J$ at $A$, then

${U}_{B} - 1560 = 40J ⇒ {U}_{B} = 1600J$

In the part $B \to C$, the work done by the gas is $W = 50J$ and no heat is given to the system. Again using $Q = \DeltaU + W$

$0 = \DeltaU - 50$ or $\DeltaU = {U}_{C} - {U}_{B} = 50J$

${U}_{C} - 1600 = 50J ⇒ {U}_{C} = 1650J$

The change in internal energy from $C \to A$,

$∆ U = 1560 - 1650 = - 90J$

The heat given to the system is $Q = - 60J$

Using $Q = \DeltaU + W$, we get $W = Q - ∆ U = - 60 - \left(- 90\right) = 30J$

43946.text: A reversible heat engine converts one-fourth of the heat input into work. When the temperature of the sink is reduced by $52K,$ its efficiency is doubled. The temperature in Kelvin of the source will be ___ .
43946.sol:
Efficiency of reversible engine is $η = \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{W}{{Q}_{in}} = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{2}}{{T}_{1}}$

From above, $\dfrac{{T}_{2}}{{T}_{1}} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

When the temperature of the sink is reduced by $52K$ then its efficiency is doubled.

Then, $\dfrac{{T}_{2} - 52}{{T}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{2}}{{T}_{1}} - \dfrac{52}{{T}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{52}{{T}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \dfrac{52}{{T}_{1}} = \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4} ⇒ {T}_{1} = 52 \times 4 = 208K$

44424.text: The distance between two consecutive points with phase difference of $60 °$ in a wave of frequency $500Hz$ is $6 . 0m$. The velocity with which wave is travelling is ______ $km{s}^{- 1}$.
44424.sol:
Distance between two consecutive points $60 °$ out of phase is given by $\Deltax = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi}\Deltaϕ$

Putting the values, we have

$6 = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

$⇒ \lambda = 36m$

Now, velocity of wave is $v = f\lambda = ( 500Hz ) ( 36m )$

$= 18000m{s}^{- 1} = 18km{s}^{- 1}$

58720.subject: Chemistry
58720.text: Which from the following metal chlorides does not contain water of crystallisation ?
58720.sol:
Alkali metal chlorides generally do not form hydrates, with the exception of lithium chloride, which is deliquescent and crystallises as a dihydrate, $\text{LiCl} \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Alkaline earth metal chlorides such as $\text{MgCl}_2$ and $\text{BeCl}_2$ readily form hydrates. $\text{MgCl}_2$ crystallises as a hexahydrate, $\text{MgCl}_2 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and $\text{BeCl}_2$ crystallises as a tetrahydrate, $\text{BeCl}_2 \cdot 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Caesium chloride ($\text{CsCl}$) is an alkali metal chloride that does not form hydrates and crystallises as an anhydrous salt.

Therefore, $\text{CsCl}$ does not contain water of crystallisation.

Answer: $\text{CsCl}$

58827.text: An ionic compound is formed by elements X and Y. Element Y forms a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice, and element X occupies one-third of the tetrahedral voids. What is the formula of the compound?
58827.sol:
Element Y forms a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice.

Number of Y atoms per unit cell = $4$

Number of tetrahedral voids in an FCC unit cell = $2 \times 4 = 8$

Element X occupies one-third of the tetrahedral voids.

Number of X atoms per unit cell = $\dfrac{1}{3} \times 8 = \dfrac{8}{3}$

Ratio of X to Y = $\dfrac{8}{3} : 4 = 8 : 12 = 2 : 3$

The formula of the compound is $X_2Y_3$.

59927.subject: Chemistry
59927.text: $Calculate work done in isothermal reversible expansion of 1 mole ideal gas from initial pressure 10 bar to final pressure 1 bar at 300 K  \left(\mathrm{R}=8.314 \mathrm{ J} \mathrm{ K}^{-1} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}\right)$
59927.sol:
The work done by an ideal gas during an isothermal reversible expansion is given by $W = -nRT \ln \left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right).

Since pressure$ and $volume vary inversely for an ideal gas at constant temperature, \frac{V_2}{V_1} = \frac{P_1}{P_2}, yielding$ W = -nRT \ln $\left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right)$.

Substituting the given values $n = 1$ mol, $R = 8.314$ J K^{-1}$ mol^{-1}$, $T = 300$ K, $P_1 = 10$ bar, and $P_2 = 1$ bar:
$W = -(1)(8.314)(300) \ln \left(\frac{10}{1}\right)<$/p>

Calculating stepwise:
$8.314 \times300 = 2494.2$
\ln(10) \approx$2.303$
$W = -2494.2 \times2.303 = -5744.1426$ J = $-5.744$ kJ

Among the options provided, $-5.74$ kJ corresponds to option C.

60220.text: If Rolle's theorem is applicable for the function $f(x) = \log \left(\dfrac{x^2+a}{x}\right) on $[3,4]$ with $c \in (3,4)$ such that $f'(c) = 0$, then the value of $f''(c)$ is$
60220.sol:
Since Rolle's theorem is applicable for $f(x)$ on $[3, 4]$, we have $f(3) = f(4)$.

$\log \left(\dfrac{9+a}{3}\right) = \log \left(\dfrac{16+a}{4}\right)

\dfrac{9+a}{3} = \dfrac{16+a}{4}

36 + 4a = 48 + 3a \Rightarrow a = 12$

The function becomes $f(x) = \log(x²+12) - \log x$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{2x}{x^2+12} - \dfrac{1}{x}

For $ f'(c) = 0$:

\dfrac{2c}{c^2+12} - \dfrac{1}{c} =0 \Rightarrow 2c^2 = c² + 12 \Rightarrow c² = 12$

Differentiating $f'(x)$ again to find $f''(x)$:

$f''(x) = \dfrac{2(x^2+12) - 2x(2x)}{(x^2+12)^2} + \dfrac{1}{x^2} = \dfrac{24-2x^2}{(x^2+12)^2} + \dfrac{1}{x^2}

Substituting $ c^2 = 12$:

$f''(c) = $\dfrac{24 - 2(12)}{(12+12)^2} + \dfrac{1}{12} =0 + \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{12}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{12}$

60229.subject: Mathematics
60229.text: A wire of length $64$ m is to be bent to form a rectangle such that its area is maximum, then its area is.....
60229.sol:
Let the length and breadth of the rectangle be $x$ and $y$ respectively.

The perimeter of the rectangle is equal to the length of the wire.

$2(x + y) = 64$

$x + y = 32$

The area of the rectangle is $A = xy$.

Using the AM-GM inequality for positive numbers $x$ and $y$:

$\dfrac{x + y}{2} \ge \sqrt{xy}$

$\dfrac{32}{2} \ge \sqrt{A}$

$16 \ge \sqrt{A}$

$A \le 256$

The maximum area of the rectangle is $256$ sq.m, which occurs when $x = y = 16$ m (when the rectangle is a square).

60262.text: Let f be a function which is continuous and differentiable for all $x$. If $\mathrm{f}(1)=1$ and $\mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x}) \leq 5$ for all $x$ in $[1,5]$, then the maximum value of $f(5)$ is
60262.sol:
Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem ensures there exists $c \in (1, 5)$ satisfying $f'(c) = \frac{f(5) - f(1)}{5 - 1}$.
Given $f(1) = 1$, this simplifies to $f'(c) = \frac{f(5) - 1}{4}$.
Since $f'(x) \leq 5$ for all $x \in [1, 5]$, and $c$ lies within this interval, $f'(c) \leq 5$.

Substituting gives $\frac{f(5) - 1}{4} \leq 5$.
Multiplying both sides by 4: $f(5) - 1 \leq 20$.
Adding 1 yields $f(5) \leq 21$, establishing the maximum possible value.

$\boxed{21}$

62012.subject: Mathematics
62012.text: The domain of the function $f(x) = \sqrt{x - 1} + \sqrt{3 - x}$ is...
62012.sol:
For the function $f(x) = \sqrt{x - 1} + \sqrt{3 - x}$ to be defined, the expressions inside the square roots must be non-negative.

$x - 1 \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \ge 1$

$3 - x \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \le 3$

Taking the intersection of both conditions, we get $1 \le x \le 3$.

Thus, the domain of the function is $[1,3]$.

Answer: $[1,3]$

62922.subject: Mathematics
62922.text: If the truth value of $[(p \vee q) \wedge (q \to r) \wedge (\sim r)] \to (p \wedge q)$ is false, then which of the following is NOT true?
options: Truth value of $p \to q$ is False
Truth value of $p \to r$ is False.
Truth value of $(\sim q) \to p$ is False.
The truth value of $(\sim p) \wedge r$ is False.
62922.sol:
Given that the truth value of $[(p \vee q) \wedge (q \to r) \wedge (\sim r)] \to (p \wedge q)$ is False.

An implication $A \to B$ is False if and only if $A$ is True and $B$ is False. Therefore, the antecedent $(p \vee q) \wedge (q \to r) \wedge (\sim r)$ is True and the consequent $p \wedge q$ is False.

For the antecedent to be True, each of its conjuncts must be True:
1) $\sim r$ is True $\Rightarrow r$ is False.
2) $q \to r$ is True. Since $r$ is False, $q$ must be False (otherwise $T \to F$ would be False).
3) $p \vee q$ is True. Since $q$ is False, $p$ must be True.

Checking the consequent: $p \wedge q \equiv T \wedge F \equiv F$, which is consistent.

Thus, the truth values are: $p$ is True, $q$ is False, and $r$ is False.

Now, evaluating the given options:
1) $p \to q \equiv T \to F \equiv F$. The statement "Truth value of $p \to q$ is False" is True.
2) $p \to r \equiv T \to F \equiv F$. The statement "Truth value of $p \to r$ is False" is True.
3) $(\sim q) \to p \equiv (\sim F) \to T \equiv T \to T \equiv T$. The statement "Truth value of $(\sim q) \to p$ is False" is False.
4) $(\sim p) \wedge r \equiv (\sim T) \wedge F \equiv F \wedge F \equiv F$. The statement "The truth value of $(\sim p) \wedge r$ is False" is True.

Therefore, the statement in the third option is NOT true.

Answer: Truth value of $(\sim q) \to p$ is False.

64490.text: The distance of the point $(-3,2,3)$ from the line passing through $(4,6,-2)$ and having direction ratios $-1,2,3$ is ________ units.
64490.sol:
The distance from point $P(-3,2,3)$ to the line through $A(4,6,-2)$ with direction vector $\vec{b} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ is determined by the formula $d = \frac{|\vec{AP} \times \vec{b}|}{|\vec{b}|}$.

The vector $\vec{AP} = P - A = -7\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$.

The cross product yields $\vec{AP} \times \vec{b} = -22\hat{i} + 16\hat{j} - 18\hat{k}$, with magnitude $|\vec{AP} \times \vec{b}| = \sqrt{484 + 256 + 324} = \sqrt{1064}$.

The magnitude of the direction vector is $|\vec{b}| = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 9} = \sqrt{14}$.

Thus, the distance becomes $d = \frac{\sqrt{1064}}{\sqrt{14}} = \sqrt{\frac{1064}{14}} = \sqrt{76} = 2\sqrt{19}$.

This corresponds to option C.

Substitute $\sin^2 \theta = 1 - \cos^2 \theta$ to form a quadratic in $\cos \theta$: $6 \cos \theta = 6 - 8(1 - \cos^2 \theta)$, which simplifies to $4 \cos^2 \theta - 3 \cos \theta - 1 = 0$.

Factor as $(4\cos\theta + 1)(\cos\theta - 1) = 0$, giving $\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{4}$ or $\cos\theta = 1$. Only $\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{4}$ lies within the domain $0 < \theta < \pi$.

Using $\sin^2 \theta = 1 - \cos^2 \theta$, compute $\sin^2 \theta = 1 - \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{15}{16}$. Since $\sin \theta > 0$ in this interval, $\sin \theta = \frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}$.

The correct option is D.

65632.text: An alternating voltage $\mathrm{E}=100 \sqrt{2} \sin (50 \mathrm{t})$ is connected to a $2 \mu \mathrm{F}$ capacitor through an a.c. ammeter. The ammeter reading will be
65632.sol:
The alternating voltage is given by $E = 100 \sqrt{2} \sin(50t)$, corresponding to a peak voltage $E_0 = 100 \sqrt{2} \text{ V}$ and angular frequency $\omega = 50 \text{ rad/s}$.

For the capacitor with capacitance $C = 2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ F}$, the capacitive reactance is $X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{50 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}} = 10^4 \ \Omega$.

The peak current is $I_0 = \frac{E_0}{X_C} = \frac{100 \sqrt{2}}{10^4} = 0.01 \sqrt{2} \text{ A}$.

Since the ammeter measures the RMS current, we compute $I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{0.01 \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 0.01 \text{ A}$. Converting to milliamperes gives $I_{\text{rms}} = 10 \text{ mA}$.

The ammeter reading is $\boxed{\text{10 mA}}$.

66042.subject: Physics
66042.text: Four capacitors are connected to a battery as shown in figure. The ratio of charges on capacitors $C_2$ and $C_4$ is
66042.sol:
From the given circuit diagram, capacitors $C_1$, $C_2$, and $C_3$ are connected in series. This series combination is connected in parallel with capacitor $C_4$ across the battery of voltage $V$.

The equivalent capacitance $C_s$ of the series branch containing $C_1$, $C_2$, and $C_3$ is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{C_s} = \dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2} + \dfrac{1}{C_3}$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{1}{C_s} = \dfrac{1}{1C} + \dfrac{1}{2C} + \dfrac{1}{3C} = \dfrac{6 + 3 + 2}{6C} = \dfrac{11}{6C}$

$C_s = \dfrac{6C}{11}$

Since $C_1$, $C_2$, and $C_3$ are in series, the charge on each of them is the same and is equal to the total charge on this series branch. The voltage across this branch is $V$.

Charge on $C_2$, $Q_2 = C_s \times V = \dfrac{6CV}{11}$

Capacitor $C_4$ is connected directly across the battery, so the voltage across it is also $V$.

Charge on $C_4$, $Q_4 = C_4 \times V = 4CV$

The ratio of charges on $C_2$ and $C_4$ is:

$\dfrac{Q_2}{Q_4} = \dfrac{\dfrac{6CV}{11}}{4CV} = \dfrac{6}{11 \times 4} = \dfrac{6}{44} = \dfrac{3}{22}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{22}$

68166.text: Two capillary tubes of same diameter are kept vertically in two liquids whose densities are in the ratio $4: 3$. If their surface tensions are in the ratio 6:5, the ratio of heights $\left(\frac{h_1}{h_2}\right)$ of liquids in the two capillary tubes is (Their angle of contacts are same)
68166.sol:
The equilibrium height $h$ for capillary action is given by the capillary rise equation:

$h = \frac{2T \cos\theta}{r \rho g}$

Since both tubes have identical diameters and angle of contact, all parameters except $T$ and $\rho$ cancel in the height ratio:

$\frac{h_1}{h_2} = \frac{T_1}{T_2} \times \frac{\rho_2}{\rho_1}$

Substituting the given ratios $\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{6}{5}$ and $\frac{\rho_1}{\rho_2} = \frac{4}{3} \implies \frac{\rho_2}{\rho_1} = \frac{3}{4}$:

$\frac{h_1}{h_2} = \frac{6}{5} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{18}{20} = \frac{9}{10}$

This corresponds to option B.

$u_1 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) =u_2 \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)

\dfrac{u_1}{u_2} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{1}

The ratio of their initial velocities is \sqrt{2}$: 1$.

68600.text: Two samples A and B contain equal amount of radioactive substances. If $\left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right)^{th}$ of sample A and $\left(\dfrac{1}{128}\right)^{th}$ of sample B, remain after 9 hours, then the ratio of half life period of B to that of A is
68600.sol:
Let the initial amount of both samples be $N_0$.

The amount of radioactive substance remaining after time $t$ is given by $N = N_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{t}{T_{1/2}}}$.

For sample A, after $t = 9$ hours:

$\dfrac{N_0}{8} = N_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{9}{T_A}}$

$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{9}{T_A}}$

$\dfrac{9}{T_A} = 3 \Rightarrow T_A = 3$ hours.

For sample B, after $t = 9$ hours:

$\dfrac{N_0}{128} = N_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{9}{T_B}}$

$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^7 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{9}{T_B}}$

$\dfrac{9}{T_B} = 7 \Rightarrow T_B = \dfrac{9}{7}$ hours.

The ratio of the half-life period of B to that of A is:

$\dfrac{T_B}{T_A} = \dfrac{\dfrac{9}{7}}{3} = \dfrac{3}{7}$

Answer: $3:7$

70125.subject: Physics
70125.text: To improve the resolving power of a compound microscope we should
options: decrease the diameter of the objective lens.
decrease the focal length of the eye-piece.
increase the refractive index of the medium between the object and objective lens.
70125.sol:
The resolving power of a compound microscope is given by the formula:

$\text{Resolving Power} = \dfrac{2 \mu \sin \theta}{\lambda}$

where $\mu$ is the refractive index of the medium between the object and the objective lens, $\theta$ is the half-angle of the cone of light from the object to the objective lens, and $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light used.

To improve or increase the resolving power, one can:
1. Increase the refractive index $\mu$ of the medium.
2. Increase the angle $\theta$ (by increasing the diameter of the objective lens).
3. Decrease the wavelength $\lambda$ of the light used.

Therefore, increasing the refractive index of the medium between the object and the objective lens will improve the resolving power.

Answer: increase the refractive index of the medium between the object and objective lens.

70918.subject: Biology
70918.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I - Ecosystem diversity is very low in India while it is quite high in Norway.
Statement II - The western ghats in India show great ecosystem diversity while regions like Ladakh and Rann of Kutch do not show variance like western ghats.
In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both, statement - I and statement - II are correct.
Both, statement - I and statement - II are incorrect.
Statement - I is correct but statement - II is incorrect.
Statement - I is incorrect but statement - II is correct.
70918.sol:
Statement I is incorrect. According to ecological data, India has a much greater ecosystem diversity than a Scandinavian country like Norway. India is characterized by a wide variety of ecosystems, including deserts, rainforests, mangroves, coral reefs, wetlands, estuaries, and alpine meadows.

Statement II is correct. The Western Ghats are recognized as a biodiversity hotspot and exhibit immense ecosystem diversity, encompassing tropical evergreen forests, moist deciduous forests, montane forests (sholas), and grasslands. In contrast, regions like Ladakh (a high-altitude cold desert) and the Rann of Kutch (a seasonal salt marsh) are extreme, relatively uniform environments that do not display the same level of ecological variance and diversity as the Western Ghats.

Therefore, Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Answer: Statement - I is incorrect but statement - II is correct.

70920.subject: Biology
70920.text:
Which of the following are the narrowly utilitarian reasons for conservation of biodiversity?
(A). For providing equal right of survival to living beings.
(B). For industrial products like resins, tannins etc.
(C). For pollination and seed dispersal.
(D). For medicinal use of plants and animals.
70920.sol:
The reasons for conserving biodiversity are classified into three categories: narrowly utilitarian, broadly utilitarian, and ethical.

Narrowly utilitarian arguments focus on the direct economic benefits derived from nature, such as food, firewood, fibre, construction material, industrial products (like tannins, lubricants, dyes, resins, perfumes), and medicinal products. Therefore, statements (B) and (D) represent narrowly utilitarian reasons.

Broadly utilitarian arguments relate to ecosystem services provided by nature, such as oxygen production, pollination, and seed dispersal. Thus, statement (C) is a broadly utilitarian reason.

Ethical arguments are based on the intrinsic value of every species and the moral duty to ensure their well-being and equal right of survival. Thus, statement (A) is an ethical reason.

Hence, only (B) and (D) are narrowly utilitarian reasons.

Answer: (B) and (D) only.

71355.subject: Biology
71355.text: The genes located on homologous regions of X and Y chromosomes do not inherit together because crossing over occurs in this region. Thus, they exhibit incomplete sex linkage. They are called the X-Y linked traits. Which of the following is NOT an example of X-Y linked traits?
71355.sol:
Genes located on the homologous regions of X and Y chromosomes are known as incompletely sex-linked genes or X-Y linked genes. Because crossing over can occur in these homologous regions, these traits do not always inherit together.

Common examples of X-Y linked traits in humans include total colour blindness, nephritis, retinitis pigmentosa, xeroderma pigmentosum, and epidermolysis bullosa.

Myopia is not an X-Y linked trait. It is generally inherited as an autosomal or X-linked trait.

Answer: Myopia.

71620.subject: Chemistry
71620.text: Which of the following reagents gives the same reduction product with propionaldehyde and acetone ?
71620.sol:
Propionaldehyde is $CH_3CH_2CHO$ and acetone is $CH_3COCH_3$.

Reduction with $LiAlH_4$, $Ni / H_2$, or $Na-Hg / HCl$ converts propionaldehyde to 1-propanol (CH_3CH_2CH_2OH$) and acetone to 2-propanol (CH_3CH(OH)CH_3$), which are different products.

Reduction with $Zn-Hg / Conc. HCl$ (Clemmensen reduction) reduces the carbonyl group to a methylene group. Thus, both propionaldehyde and acetone are reduced to propane (CH_3CH_2CH_3$), giving the same product.

72253.subject: Physics
72253.text:
An electron is projected with uniform velocity along the axis of a current carrying long solenoid. Which of the following is true?
a. The electron will be accelerated along the axis.
b. The electron path will be circular about the axis.
c. The electron will experience a force at $45^\circ$ to the axis and hence execute a helical path.
d. The electron will continue to move with uniform velocity along the axis of the solenoid.
72253.sol:
The magnetic field inside a long current-carrying solenoid is uniform and directed along its axis.

The electron is projected with a uniform velocity along the axis of the solenoid, which means its velocity vector $\vec{v}$ is parallel or anti-parallel to the magnetic field vector $\vec{B}$.

The magnetic force experienced by a moving charge is given by $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$.

Since the angle $\theta$ between $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{B}$ is either $0^\circ$ or $180^\circ$, the cross product $\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = vB\sin\theta = 0$.

Therefore, the magnetic force acting on the electron is zero. In the absence of any force, the electron will not accelerate and will continue to move with its initial uniform velocity along the axis of the solenoid.

Answer: d

76708.subject: Mathematics
76708.text:
Consider the following statements in respect of $f(x)=|x|-1$ :
1. $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$.
2. $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=0$.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
76708.sol:
Here, $f(x)=|x|-1\therefore f(x)\left\{\begin{array}{cc}
-x-1, & x < 0 \\
x-1, & x \geq 0
\end{array}\right.$
For continuity at $x=1$.
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{LHL}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{-}}(x-1)=1-1=0 \\
& \mathrm{RHL}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{+}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{+}}(x-1)=1-1=0
\end{aligned}\therefore f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$.
For differentiability at $x=0$.
$\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime}(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}
-1, & x < 0 \\
1, & x \geq 0
\end{array}\right. \\
& \mathrm{LHD}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} f^{\prime}(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}}(-1)=-1 \\
& \mathrm{RHD}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f^{\prime}(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}(1)=1
\end{aligned}\therefore f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x=0$

77319.subject: Mathematics
77319.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $f = \{(1,1), (2,4), (3,7), (4,10)\}$.

Consider the following statements:
I. $f$ is one-one function.
II. $f$ is onto function if the codomain is the set of natural numbers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77319.sol:
The given function is $f = \{(1,1), (2,4), (3,7), (4,10)\}$.

The domain of $f$ is $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ and the range of $f$ is $\{1, 4, 7, 10\}$.

Since each element in the domain has a distinct image in the range, $f$ is a one-one function. Statement I is correct.

If the codomain is the set of natural numbers, the range $\{1, 4, 7, 10\}$ is a proper subset of the codomain. Since the range is not equal to the codomain, $f$ is not an onto function. Statement II is incorrect.

Therefore, only Statement I is correct.

Answer: I only

Each of the chromatids is capped with the telomere structure on either end of each arm. Therefore, a single chromosome in metaphase would have four total telomeres, two on each sister chromatid. iv) Phosphorous released in the process becomes available for reutilization of plants.

82387.text: In the circuits shown below, the readings of the voltmeters and the ammeters will be,
82387.sol:
For an ideal voltmeter, resistance is infinite $\left({R}_{V} = \infty\right)$, so it will not draw any amount of current from the circuit and for ideal ammeter resistance is zero.

Then for the first figure ${R}_{1} = 10Ω, {R}_{V} = \infty$ and both are in a parallel arrangement, so

$\dfrac{1}{{R}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{{R}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{R}_{V}} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{{R}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{\infty} ⇒ {R}_{eq} = 10Ω$

and current in the first circuit is, ${i}_{1} = \dfrac{{V}_{1}}{{R}_{eq}} = \dfrac{10}{10} = 1A$

So, for the first circuit, ammeter and voltmeter readings are ${V}_{1} = 10V, {i}_{1} = 1A$, respectively.

For the second figure voltmeter and resistant of $10Ω$ are in series and also connected parallel to another resistant of $10Ω$. So, equivalent resistant is

$\dfrac{1}{{R}^{'}eq} = \dfrac{1}{{R}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{R}_{2} + {R}_{V}} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{{R}^{'}eq} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{10 + \infty} = \dfrac{1}{10} + 0 = \dfrac{1}{10} ⇒ {R}^{'}eq = 10Ω$

$∴$ Current in the circuit is, ${i}_{2} = {V}_{2}{R}_{eq}^{'} = \dfrac{10}{10} = 1A$,

$∴$ Ammeter and voltmeter readings for the second circuit is ${V}_{2} = 10V, {i}_{2} = 1A$

$∴$ For both the circuit is
${V}_{1} = {V}_{2} = 10V, {i}_{1} = {i}_{2} = 1A$

84253.text: The blood calcium level is lowered by the deficiency of
84253.sol:
The chief cells of the parathyroids secrete parathormone. Its deficiency causes the lowering of blood calcium level. This increases the excitability of nerves and muscles causing cramps and convulsions. This caused parathyroid tetany characterised by sustained contractions of the muscles of larynx, face, hands and feet.
Calcitonin is secreted when calcium level is high in blood. It has an opposite action to that of parathyroid hormone and lowers the calcium level by suppressing release of calcium ions from the bones.
Thyroxine is secreted from the thyroid gland. It regulates the metabolic rate of the body and thus, maintain basal metobolic rate, stimulate protein synthesis and therefore, promote growth of the body tissues.

84305.sol:
• Salivary glands are one of the most important glands in our digestive systems which produces saliva. Saliva contains a carbohydrate digesting enzyme called salivary amylase (ptyalin). 84625.subject: Zoology
84625.text: Several hormones like hCG, hPL, estrogen, progesterone are produced by
84625.sol:
Hormones secreted by the placenta are hCG, hPL, oestrogen, and progesterone. Human chorionic gonadotropin hormone (hCG). This hormone is only produced during pregnancy almost exclusively in the placenta. HCG hormone levels found in maternal blood and urine increase dramatically during the first trimester and may contribute to causing nausea and vomiting often associated with pregnancy.

Human placental lactogen (hPL). This hormone, produced by the placenta, helps in the process of providing nutrition for the foetus and plays a role in stimulating milk glands in the breasts in anticipation of breastfeeding.

Oestrogen. This group of hormones is responsible for the development of female sexual characteristics. Normally formed in the ovaries, oestrogen is also produced by the placenta during pregnancy to help maintain a healthy pregnancy.

Progesterone. This hormone is produced by the ovaries and by the placenta during pregnancy. Progesterone stimulates the thickening of the uterine lining in anticipation of the implantation of a fertilised egg.

85324.text: In mutational event, when adenine is replaced by guanine. it is a case of:
85324.sol: Point mutations are those mutations that affect a single base pair. The most common nucleotide mutations are substitutions, in which one base is replaced by another. These can be of two types, either transitions or transversions. Transition substitution refers to a purine or pyrimidine being replaced by a base of the same kind; for example, a purine such as adenine may be replaced by the purine guanine. Transversion substitution refers to a purine being replaced by a pyrimidine, or vice versa; for example, cytosine, a pyrimidine, is replaced by adenine, a purine. A frameshift mutation occurs due to an insertion or deletion of a base pair that are usually not in the multiples of three. It causes the transformation of the genetic code in an unreadable format or a reading frame from the location of the mutation up till the end of the gene. Number of ways of selecting seats $= {}^{n + r - 1}{C}_{r - 1} = {}^{3 + 5 - 1}{C}_{3 - 1} = {}^{7}{C}_{2}$
Persons can interchange their seats in $2 ! \times 2 !$ ways

&

Using (i),

$\text{v} = \dfrac{\text{r} \sqrt{\text{g}}}{{\left(L^{2} - r^{2}\right)}^{1/4}} \text{and} \text{T} = \dfrac{\text{mgL}}{{\left(L^{2} - r^{2}\right)}^{1/2}}$

94494.sol:
For two bodies made up of same material, rate of loss of heat will depend only on their surface area for same temperature change.

$∴ \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{dQ}{dt}\right)}_{1}}{{\left(\dfrac{dQ}{dt}\right)}_{2}} = \dfrac{{A}_{1}}{{A}_{2}} = {r}_{1}^{2}{r}_{2}^{2} \ldots \ldots \left(i\right)$

Ratio of initial rates of cooling$= \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\right)}_{1}}{{\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\right)}_{2}}$

As, $\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = mc\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$

$∴ \dfrac{{m}_{1}{c}_{1} ( d\theta / dt{)}_{1}}{{m}_{2}{c}_{2} ( d\theta / dt{)}_{2}} = {r}_{1}^{2}{r}_{2}^{2}$ ...[from (i)]

since, both the spheres are made up of copper,

${c}_{1} = {c}_{2} = c$.

$∴ \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\right)}_{1}}{{\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\right)}_{2}} = \dfrac{{r}_{1}^{2} \times {m}_{2}}{{r}_{2}^{2} \times {m}_{1}}$

As, spheres have same densities,

$\dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}} = \dfrac{{V}_{1}}{{V}_{2}} = {r}_{1}^{3}{r}_{2}^{3}$

$∴ \dfrac{( d\theta / dt{)}_{1}}{( d\theta / dt{)}_{2}} = {r}_{1}^{2}{r}_{2}^{2} \times {r}_{2}^{3}{r}_{1}^{3} = \dfrac{{r}_{2}}{{r}_{1}} = \dfrac{20}{15} = \dfrac{4}{3} = 1 . 33$

[I] In a flowering plant the substances that would need to be transported are water, mineral nutrients, organic nutrients and plant growth regulators.
[II] Over small distances, substances move by diffusion and by cytoplasmic streaming supplemented only by passive transport.

101392.subject: Physics
101392.text: A satellite A revolves around a planet of radius $R$ at a height $R$ from its surface. Its time period of revolution is $T$. Another satellite B revolves around the same planet with a time period of $8T$. What is the height of satellite B from the surface of the planet?
101392.sol:
According to Kepler's third law, the square of the time period is proportional to the cube of the orbital radius: $T^2 \propto r^3$, which gives $T \propto r^{3/2}$.

Let $r_A$ and $r_B$ be the orbital radii of satellites A and B respectively.
The orbital radius of satellite A is $r_A = R + h_A = R + R = 2R$.

Taking the ratio of their time periods:
$\dfrac{T_B}{T_A} = \left(\dfrac{r_B}{r_A}\right)^{3/2}$

Given $T_A = T$ and $T_B = 8T$:
$\dfrac{8T}{T} = \left(\dfrac{r_B}{2R}\right)^{3/2}$

$8 = \left(\dfrac{r_B}{2R}\right)^{3/2}$

Raising both sides to the power of $2/3$:
$\dfrac{r_B}{2R} = (8)^{2/3} = 4$

$r_B = 4 \times 2R = 8R$

The height of satellite B from the surface is:
$h_B = r_B - R = 8R - R = 7R$.

Answer: $7R$

103122.subject: Physics
103122.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a fully charged capacitor is connected to a steady DC battery, the displacement current between its plates is zero.

Reason (R): The displacement current between the plates of a capacitor is directly proportional to the steady electric potential difference applied across it.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
103122.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: When a capacitor is fully charged by a steady DC battery, the potential difference across its plates becomes constant with time ($\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 0$). Since displacement current is given by $I_d = C \dfrac{dV}{dt}$, it becomes zero under steady DC conditions.

Reason (R) is false: Displacement current is not proportional to the steady electric potential difference itself. Instead, it is directly proportional to the rate of change of electric potential difference with time ($\dfrac{dV}{dt}$).

Therefore, Assertion is true but Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

103346.subject: Physics
103346.text: When a galvanometer is shunted with a resistance $S$, it is found that only $5\%$ of the main circuit current passes through the galvanometer coil. The resistance of the galvanometer ($G$) in terms of the shunt resistance ($S$) is :
103346.sol:
Let the main circuit current be $I$.

The current passing through the galvanometer is $I_g = 5\% of I = \dfrac{5}{100}I = \dfrac{I}{20}$.

In a shunted galvanometer, the galvanometer and the shunt resistance are in parallel. The potential difference across them is equal:

$I_g G = (I - I_g) S$

Substituting $I_g = \dfrac{I}{20}$:

$\left(\dfrac{I}{20}\right) G = \left(I - \dfrac{I}{20}\right) S$

$\dfrac{I}{20} G = \dfrac{19I}{20} S$

Cancelling $\dfrac{I}{20}$ from both sides:

$G = 19S$

Answer: $19S$

104294.text:
An LC circuit is used as a transmitter to generate electromagnetic waves in free space. If the circuit contains an inductor of inductance $L = \dfrac{2.5}{\pi^2}$ mH and a capacitor of capacitance $C = 1$ $\mu$F, what is the wavelength of the emitted electromagnetic wave?
(Take the speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s)
104294.sol:
The frequency of the emitted electromagnetic wave is equal to the resonant frequency of the oscillating charge in the LC circuit.

The resonant frequency is given by:
$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi \sqrt{LC}}$

Given $L = \dfrac{2.5}{\pi^2} \times 10^{-3}$ H and $C = 10^{-6}$ F, we have:
$LC = \dfrac{2.5 \times 10^{-9}}{\pi^2} = \dfrac{25 \times 10^{-10}}{\pi^2}$

$\sqrt{LC} = \dfrac{5 \times 10^{-5}}{\pi}$ s

Substituting this into the frequency formula:
$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi \left( \dfrac{5 \times 10^{-5}}{\pi} \right)} = \dfrac{1}{10 \times 10^{-5}} = 10^4$ Hz

The wavelength $\lambda$ of the electromagnetic wave in free space is:
$\lambda = \dfrac{c}{f} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{10^4} = 3 \times 10^4$ m

Answer: $3 \times 10^4$ m

104705.text: A Young's double slit apparatus produces interference fringes of width $1.2 \mathrm{~mm}$ on a screen when the experiment is performed in air. If the entire apparatus is immersed in a transparent liquid of refractive index $\dfrac{4}{3}$, the new fringe width will be
104705.sol:
The fringe width in air is given by $\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$

When the entire apparatus is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $\mu$, the wavelength of light in the liquid becomes $\lambda' = \dfrac{\lambda}{\mu}$.

The new fringe width $\beta'$ is:
$\beta' = \dfrac{\lambda' D}{d} = \dfrac{\lambda D}{\mu d} = \dfrac{\beta}{\mu}$

Substitute the given values:
$\beta = 1.2 \mathrm{~mm}$
$\mu = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$\beta' = \dfrac{1.2}{\dfrac{4}{3}} = 1.2 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.9 \mathrm{~mm}$

Answer: $0.9 \mathrm{~mm}$

Match List-I with List-II for an unpolarised light beam incident on a transparent medium at Brewster's angle ($i_p$).

List-IList-II
(A) Angle between reflected and refracted rays(I) Partially polarised

104727.sol:
According to Brewster's law, when unpolarised light is incident at the polarising angle ($i_p$), the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other. Hence, the angle between them is $90^\circ$.

The refractive index of the medium is given by $\mu = \tan(i_p)$.

At this angle of incidence, the reflected ray is completely plane-polarised, whereas the refracted ray is partially polarised.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)

105238.text: A logic circuit provides the output $Y$ as per the following truth table :$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline A & B & Y \\\hline 0 & 0 & 0 \\0 & 1 & 1 \\1 & 0 & 0 \\1 & 1 & 0 \\\hline\end{array}Which of the following logic gate arrangements corresponds to this truth table?$
options: Input $A$ is connected to a NOT gate, and its output is fed to an AND gate along with input $B$.
Input $B$ is connected to a NOT gate, and its output is fed to an AND gate along with input $A$.
Inputs $A$ and $B$ are fed to an AND gate, and its output is connected to a NOT gate.
Input $A$ is connected to a NOT gate, and its output is fed to an OR gate along with input $B$.
105238.sol:
From the given truth table, the output $Y$ is $1$ only when $A = 0$ and $B = 1$.

This means the Boolean expression for the output is $Y = \bar{A} \cdot B$.

To realize this expression using basic logic gates, input $A$ must first be inverted using a NOT gate (giving $\bar{A}$), and then this inverted signal must be combined with input $B$ using an AND gate.

Therefore, the correct arrangement is: Input $A$ is connected to a NOT gate, and its output is fed to an AND gate along with input $B$.

Answer: Input $A$ is connected to a NOT gate, and its output is fed to an AND gate along with input $B$.

105595.text: In a photoelectric experiment, the stopping potential for a certain metal surface is $1.5 \mathrm{~V}$. If the work function of the metal is $2.5 \mathrm{eV}$, the energy of the incident photons is:
105595.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation:

$E = K_{\max} + \phi$

The maximum kinetic energy $K_{\max}$ in electron-volts is numerically equal to the stopping potential in volts. Thus, for a stopping potential of $1.5 \mathrm{~V}$, the maximum kinetic energy is:

Given the work function $\phi = 2.5 \mathrm{eV}$, the energy of the incident photons is:

105613.subject: Physics
105613.text: Two monochromatic light sources, A and B, emit photons at the exact same rate. If the ratio of the power delivered by source A to that of source B is $3 : 4$, what is the ratio of their respective wavelengths, $\lambda_A : \lambda_B$?
105613.sol:
The power $P$ delivered by a light source is given by $P = n \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$, where $n$ is the number of photons emitted per second, $h$ is Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light, and $\lambda$ is the wavelength.

For source A: $P_A = n_A \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_A}$

For source B: $P_B = n_B \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_B}$

Since both sources emit photons at the same rate, $n_A = n_B$.

Therefore, the power is inversely proportional to the wavelength: $P \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda}$.

The ratio of their wavelengths is $\dfrac{\lambda_A}{\lambda_B} = \dfrac{P_B}{P_A}$.

Given that $\dfrac{P_A}{P_B} = \dfrac{3}{4}$, we get $\dfrac{\lambda_A}{\lambda_B} = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

Answer: $4 : 3$

105914.text:
An organic compound contains $54.55 \%$ of carbon, $9.09 \%$ of hydrogen and the remaining percentage of oxygen. The vapour density of the compound is $44$. The molecular formula of the compound is :
(Given atomic masses : $\mathrm{C} = 12 \text{ u}, \mathrm{H} = 1 \text{ u}, \mathrm{O} = 16 \text{ u}$)
105914.sol:
Percentage of Oxygen $= 100 - (54.55 + 9.09) = 36.36 \%$

Calculation of relative number of moles:
For C : $\dfrac{54.55}{12} = 4.54$
For H : $\dfrac{9.09}{1} = 9.09$
For O : $\dfrac{36.36}{16} = 2.27$

Simplest molar ratio (dividing by the smallest value, $2.27$):
C : $\dfrac{4.54}{2.27} = 2$
H : $\dfrac{9.09}{2.27} = 4$
O : $\dfrac{2.27}{2.27} = 1$

The empirical formula is $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4\mathrm{O}$.
Empirical formula mass $= (2 \times 12) + (4 \times 1) + (1 \times 16) = 44 \text{ u}$.

Molar mass $= 2 \times \text{Vapour density} = 2 \times 44 = 88 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Multiplying factor $n = \dfrac{\text{Molar mass}}{\text{Empirical formula mass}} = \dfrac{88}{44} = 2$.

Molecular formula $= (\text{Empirical formula}) \times n = (\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4\mathrm{O})_2 = \mathrm{C}_4\mathrm{H}_8\mathrm{O}_2$.

Answer: $\mathrm{C}_4\mathrm{H}_8\mathrm{O}_2$

107783.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Chemical Species)List-II (Individual Oxidation States of non-oxygen atoms)
A. $\text{Br}_3\text{O}_8$I. $+5$ and $0$
B. $\text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}$II. $+2$ and $0$
C. $\text{C}_3\text{O}_2$III. $+6$
D. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$IV. $+6$ and $+4$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
107783.sol:
According to the structures of molecules with fractional average oxidation states:

$\text{Br}_3\text{O}_8$ (Tribromooctaoxide) consists of a linear chain of three bromine atoms. The terminal bromine atoms are bonded to three oxygen atoms each (oxidation state $+6$), and the central bromine atom is bonded to two oxygen atoms (oxidation state $+4$).

$\text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}$ (Tetrathionate ion) has two terminal sulfur atoms bonded to three oxygen atoms each (oxidation state $+5$), and two central sulfur atoms bonded only to other sulfur atoms (oxidation state $0$).

$\text{C}_3\text{O}_2$ (Carbon suboxide) has the structure $\text{O=C=C=C=O}$. The terminal carbon atoms are bonded to one oxygen atom each (oxidation state $+2$), and the central carbon atom is bonded only to other carbon atoms (oxidation state $0$).

$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$ (Caro's acid) contains a peroxide linkage ($\text{-O-O-}$). The central sulfur atom is bonded to two oxygen atoms via double bonds, one $\text{-OH}$ group, and one $\text{-O-OH}$ group, resulting in an oxidation state of $+6$.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

109377.subject: Chemistry
109377.text:
Equal volumes of $0.20\text{ M}$ ammonium hydroxide and $0.02\text{ M}$ ammonium chloride solutions are mixed together. What will be the $\text{pH}$ of the resulting solution?
[Given: $\text{pK}_\text{b}$ of $\text{NH}_4\text{OH} = 4.75$]
109377.sol:
The mixture of a weak base ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) and its salt with a strong acid ($\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$) forms a basic buffer.

According to the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for a basic buffer:
$\text{pOH} = \text{pK}_\text{b} + \log \dfrac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]}$

Since equal volumes of the two solutions are mixed, the ratio of their concentrations in the mixture is equal to the ratio of their initial molarities.
$[\text{salt}] = 0.02\text{ M}$
$[\text{base}] = 0.20\text{ M}$

$\text{pOH} = 4.75 + \log \left(\dfrac{0.02}{0.20}\right)$
$\text{pOH} = 4.75 + \log (0.1)$
$\text{pOH} = 4.75 - 1 = 3.75$

The question asks for the $\text{pH}$ of the solution:
$\text{pH} = 14 - \text{pOH}$
$\text{pH} = 14 - 3.75 = 10.25$

Answer: $10.25$

111923.subject: Chemistry
111923.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Enantiomers(I) Optically inactive due to internal compensation
(B) Racemic mixture(II) Complete inversion of configuration
(C) Meso compound(III) Non-superimposable mirror images
(D) $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ reaction(IV) Optically inactive due to external compensation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
111923.sol:
Enantiomers (A) are stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other, matching with (III).

A racemic mixture (B) contains equal amounts of two enantiomers, and their optical rotations cancel each other out. Thus, it is optically inactive due to external compensation, matching with (IV).

A meso compound (C) contains chiral centers but has an internal plane of symmetry, making the molecule achiral overall. It is optically inactive due to internal compensation, matching with (I).

An $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ reaction (D) proceeds with the nucleophile attacking from the side opposite to the leaving group, leading to complete inversion of configuration, matching with (II).

Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

111927.subject: Chemistry
111927.text: Consider the molecule 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)phenol. When this compound is treated with one equivalent of a dilute strong acid, which site is preferentially protonated?
options: The oxygen atom of the phenolic $-OH$ group
The carbon atoms of the benzene ring
The oxygen atom of the aliphatic $-OH$ group
111927.sol:
The molecule 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)phenol contains two types of hydroxyl groups: a phenolic $-OH$ and an aliphatic primary $-OH$.

Protonation requires the availability of a lone pair of electrons on the oxygen atom. In the phenolic $-OH$ group, the lone pairs on oxygen are delocalized into the benzene ring through resonance ($+R$ effect), making them less available to accept a proton.

In the aliphatic $-OH$ group, the lone pairs are localized and their electron density is slightly enhanced by the $+I$ effect of the alkyl chain. Therefore, the aliphatic $-OH$ group is significantly more basic and will be preferentially protonated.

Answer: The oxygen atom of the aliphatic $-OH$ group

113895.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A mixture of carbon disulfide and acetone shows positive deviation from Raoult's law.
Reason (R): In this mixture, the solute-solvent (A-B) dipolar interactions are weaker than the solute-solute (A-A) and solvent-solvent (B-B) interactions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
113895.sol:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct statements.

In a mixture of carbon disulfide and acetone, the carbon disulfide molecules get between the acetone molecules and break the dipole-dipole interactions between them. As a result, the new solute-solvent (A-B) interactions are weaker than the original solute-solute (A-A) and solvent-solvent (B-B) interactions.

Because the intermolecular forces are weakened, the molecules have a higher escaping tendency, which increases the vapour pressure of the solution above the value predicted by Raoult's law. Thus, the solution shows a positive deviation, and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

114898.subject: Chemistry
114898.text: For a hypothetical chemical reaction, the activation energy is zero. If $k_1$ and $k_2$ are the rate constants of this reaction at temperatures $T_1$ and $T_2$ respectively (where $T_2 > T_1$), which of the following relationships is correct?
114898.sol:
According to the Arrhenius equation, the relationship between rate constants at two different temperatures is given by:

$\log \left(\dfrac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left(\dfrac{1}{T_1} - \dfrac{1}{T_2}\right)$

Given that the activation energy ($E_a$) is zero, substituting $E_a = 0$ into the above equation yields:

$\log \left(\dfrac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = 0$

Taking the antilog on both sides gives:

$\dfrac{k_2}{k_1} = 1 \implies k_2 = k_1$

Thus, for a reaction with zero activation energy, the rate constant is independent of temperature.

Answer: $k_2 = k_1$

117085.subject: Chemistry
117085.text: Identify the INCORRECT pairing of a $3\text{d}$ series metal's unique property and the magnetic characteristic of its specified ion.
options: Zinc: Not considered a transition metal; its $+2$ ion is diamagnetic.
Scandium: Does not show variable oxidation states; its $+3$ ion is diamagnetic.
Copper: Its $+1$ ion undergoes disproportionation in aqueous solution; its $+2$ ion is paramagnetic.
Manganese: Shows the maximum number of oxidation states in the $3\text{d}$ series; its $+2$ ion has $4$ unpaired electrons.
117085.sol:
Option 1 is a correct pairing: Zinc ($3\text{d}^{10} 4\text{s}^{2}$) is not considered a transition metal because it has completely filled d-orbitals in its ground state and its common $+2$ oxidation state. The $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ion ($3\text{d}^{10}$) has no unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic.

Option 2 is a correct pairing: Scandium only shows a $+3$ oxidation state and does not exhibit variable oxidation states. The $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ ion ($3\text{d}^{0}$) is diamagnetic.

Option 3 is a correct pairing: Copper(I) undergoes disproportionation in aqueous solution ($2\text{Cu}^{+} \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{Cu}$). The $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ion ($3\text{d}^{9}$) has one unpaired electron and is paramagnetic.

Option 4 is the incorrect pairing: While Manganese does show the maximum number of oxidation states (up to $+7$) in the $3\text{d}$ series, its $+2$ ion ($\text{Mn}^{2+}$) has the electronic configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^{5}$. Therefore, it has $5$ unpaired electrons, not $4$.

Answer: Manganese: Shows the maximum number of oxidation states in the $3\text{d}$ series; its $+2$ ion has $4$ unpaired electrons.

117114.subject: Chemistry
117114.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The absorption spectra of lanthanoid ions consist of sharp, narrow bands in the UV-visible region.

Statement II: The narrow bands are a result of strong interactions between $4f$ electrons and the surrounding ligand field.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
117114.sol:
Statement I is correct because the electronic spectra of lanthanoid ions exhibit sharp, line-like narrow absorption bands primarily due to $f-f$ transitions.

Statement II is incorrect. The $4f$ orbitals in lanthanoids are deeply buried and effectively shielded by the outer $5s$ and $5p$ electrons. As a result, the $4f$ electrons interact very weakly with the surrounding ligand field. This weak interaction and shielding are precisely why the absorption bands remain narrow and sharp, unlike the broad bands seen in transition metals.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

118821.subject: Chemistry
118821.text:
In the following reaction sequence, X and Z respectively are :
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2-\text{OH} + \text{PCl}_5 \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + X + \text{HCl}$
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{alc. KOH}} Y \xrightarrow[(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO})_2\text{O}_2]{\text{HBr}} Z$
118821.sol:
Reaction of primary alcohol with $\text{PCl}_5$ gives alkyl chloride, $\text{POCl}_3$, and $\text{HCl}$.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{PCl}_5 \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$

Thus, $X = \text{POCl}_3$.

Dehydrohalogenation of 1-chloropropane with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ yields propene.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}, \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$

Thus, $Y = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$.

Addition of $\text{HBr}$ to propene in the presence of peroxide follows anti-Markovnikov addition.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \xrightarrow{(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO})_2\text{O}_2} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$

Thus, $Z = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$.

Answer: $X = \text{POCl}_3$; $Z = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2-\text{Br}$

119895.subject: Chemistry
119895.text: Compound A (a primary aliphatic amine) reacts with $\text{HNO}_2$ at $273\text{ K}$ to give a gas B and an organic compound C. Compound D (a primary aromatic amine) reacts with $\text{HNO}_2$ at $273\text{ K}$ to form a stable salt E. Salt E on warming with water yields an organic compound F. What are the general classes of compounds C and F respectively?
options: C is an alcohol and F is a phenol
C is an alcohol and F is an alcohol
C is an alkane and F is a phenol
C is an alcohol and F is an aryl chloride
119895.sol:
When a primary aliphatic amine (Compound A) reacts with nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$) at $273\text{ K}$, it forms a highly unstable aliphatic diazonium salt that immediately decomposes to yield an alcohol (Compound C) and nitrogen gas (Gas B).

When a primary aromatic amine (Compound D) reacts with $\text{HNO}_2$ at $273\text{ K}$, it undergoes diazotization to form a stable arenediazonium salt (Salt E).

Upon warming with water, the arenediazonium salt (Salt E) undergoes hydrolysis to form a phenol (Compound F) and releases nitrogen gas.

Thus, C is an alcohol and F is a phenol.

Answer: C is an alcohol and F is a phenol
